facts: The Sunshine Protection Act passed the House 308 to 117. July 14, 2026. The Senate passed the same idea by unanimous consent in 2022; that time the House never voted.
The Senate has 14 session days before it leaves. 12 in September, 2 in October. It adjourns October 2 and returns November 9. Clocks fall back November 1.
Trump: 'Saving Daylight' gives a longer, brighter day. His stated position. Sleep doctors want the opposite: permanent standard time, which matches the body clock better.
The US already tried it in 1974. It lasted a year. Year-round daylight time began January 6, 1974, to save fuel in the oil embargo.
Support fell from 79% to 42% in three months. After morning crashes killed schoolchildren walking in the dark, including eight in Florida. Congress ended it in 1975.
19 states have laws ready to switch. Texas, Florida, Georgia, Washington, Oregon and Colorado among them. They need Congress to say yes.
Hawaii and most of Arizona never change. The Navajo Nation inside Arizona does. Five US territories stay on standard time too.
It started in 1918, and the dates keep moving. Standard Time Act, March 19, 1918. National rules came in 1966; a 2005 law added four to five weeks.
